name: UX Designer and Web Developer
description: ⚠⚠⚠ Web and digital interface designers earn $104,000 against graphic designers' $62,960 — $41,040 for closely related skill pointed at screens rather than print, and BLS expects one to grow and the other to shrink. ⚠⚠ Florida awards 1,133 credentials in this CIP family and NOT ONE is a bachelor's, while BLS gives a bachelor's as the typical entry. The degree-holders came from somewhere else.
credentialNote: ⚠⚠ NOTHING IS LICENSED, THE PORTFOLIO IS THE CREDENTIAL, AND THE DEGREE IS NOT WHERE YOU THINK IT IS. BLS gives the typical entry-level education for web developers and digital interface designers as a bachelor's degree — but Florida's web and computer graphics CIP family awards 1,133 credentials a year and none of them is a bachelor's. ⚠ 661 are certificates of twelve weeks to a year, 368 are associate degrees, 96 are longer certificates. The bachelor's-holders in this occupation came through computer science, digital arts or digital communication and media. ⚠⚠⚠ BLS'S OWN AI LANGUAGE IS WORTH READING CLOSELY HERE, BECAUSE IT IS MILDER THAN ON THE DESIGN SIDE: "improving web development tools and increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) for web development may soften the employment growth of these workers. These tools may make these workers more productive, and it may also allow some workers in other occupations to do basic web development tasks." ⚠⚠ That is SOFTEN THE GROWTH, on an occupation still projected to grow, against "reduce the need for these workers" on graphic design, which is projected to shrink. ⚠ The second sentence matters as much as the first: basic web work moving to people in other occupations is exactly what has already happened to simple site building, and it is why the defensible position in this field is applications rather than pages. ⚠ 13% of digital interface designers are self-employed, so for a minority this is a freelance business with all that implies.
bodyHtml:
⚠⚠⚠ $41,040 for pointing the same skill at a screen

RoleSOC2025 medianGrowth 2025–35
✅ Web and digital interface designer15-1255✅ $104,000✅ 5% — faster than average
Web developer15-1254$92,650
⚠ Graphic designer27-1024⚠ $62,960⚠⚠ −2%

⚠⚠⚠ The design skills overlap substantially. The money does not, and neither does the direction of travel. If you are choosing a design education in Florida and the medium is genuinely open to you, this is the most consequential table on the site's creative pages.

The occupation is 132,700 jobs with about 8,000 openings a year, 13% self-employed, and BLS gives the typical entry as a bachelor's degree.

⚠⚠⚠ BLS has three different registers for AI, and they line up

Reading the federal handbook across three occupations this site now covers:

OccupationProjectionWhat BLS says about automation
Medical records specialist✅ +8%automation noted; no dampening claimed
Web developer / digital interface designer✅ +5%AI “may soften the employment growth of these workers”
⚠ Graphic designer⚠⚠ −2%AI “projected to… reduce the need for these workers”

⚠⚠ Those are three deliberately different phrasings from the same agency, and they track how routine the output is. Where the product is a finished artefact that a tool can now generate, the language is “reduce the need”. Where it is a working system someone has to specify, build and maintain, it is “soften the growth”. Where the work is checking, auditing and defending a decision, there is no dampening claim at all.

⚠⚠⚠ That is the most useful thing a student can take from the AI question, and it is more informative than any forecast about the technology: the exposure is to the routine PRODUCTION half of a job, not to the job. Position yourself on the specification and judgement side of whatever you choose.

⚠ And read BLS's second sentence here, which people skip: AI “may also allow some workers in other occupations to do basic web development tasks.” That has already happened to simple site building — which is precisely why the defensible ground is applications rather than pages.

⚠⚠⚠ A CIP family with no bachelor's degree in it

CodeFL public institutionsCredentialsBachelor's
Computer Graphics (11.0803)18855 — 661 short certificates, 194 associate⚠⚠ 0
Web and Multimedia (11.0801)32269 — 173 associate, 96 certificates⚠⚠ 0
Modeling and Simulation (11.0804)290

⚠⚠⚠ 1,133 credentials and not one bachelor's, in an occupation whose typical entry BLS gives as a bachelor's. The graduates holding degrees came through computer science, digital arts or digital communication and media instead.

⚠⚠ Which is not a reason to dismiss the certificates. 32 institutions carry the web and multimedia code and Valencia alone awards 276 computer graphics credentials — these are cheap, local, and in a portfolio field they get you making things. But know what they are: the tier beneath the degree, not the degree.

⚠⚠ The subject has no home prefix either

Measured across the whole Florida course file, 181 distinct active course identifiers carry “web”, “user interface”, “user experience” or “human-computer” in their statewide titles — across 25 DIFFERENT PREFIXES.

Most widely carriedInstitutions
CTS0085 Web Security Specialist (150 hours)13
COP2830 Basic Web Page Programming8
DIG0083 Multimedia Web Interactive Designer (300 hours)8
CTS0070 Web Design Fundamentals (150 hours)7
CTS0071 Web Interface Design (150 hours)7

⚠⚠⚠ Not one reaches 14 carriers, and the top of the list is clock-hour technical-college training. Set that against HSC0003 at 55 carriers or PSY2012 at 33 — this subject is genuinely homeless in the Florida catalogue.

⚠ The practical consequence: you will assemble this education rather than enrol in it, and transfer credit will be difficult because no two institutions number it the same way. Keep syllabi for everything.

Necessary skills

  • Interaction design — what happens when someone clicks, and what happens when they click the wrong thing.
  • Research with actual users. The discipline that distinguishes UX from decoration, and the part no tool generates for you.
  • Enough front-end code to build what you design. BLS's warning is about basic tasks moving to others; the answer is to do the non-basic ones.
  • Accessibility, which is both a legal requirement for public-sector work and the clearest marker of a professional.
  • Systems thinking — components, states, edge cases — because a design that only covers the happy path is not finished.
  • Portfolio narrative. In a field with no licence, being able to explain the problem and the decisions is the credential.

Advice

⚠⚠⚠ If you are weighing graphic design against interface design, weigh the $41,040 and the direction. $104,000 and growing against $62,960 and shrinking, for closely related skill. That is the clearest single decision in this cluster.

⚠⚠ Get the degree from a computing or digital media programme, not this CIP family. It awards no bachelor's at all in Florida, and BLS says a bachelor's is the typical entry.

⚠ Use the certificates for what they are good at. 32 institutions, cheap, local, and they get you building. CTS0070, CTS0071 and COP2830 are the ones with the widest reach. Stack them under a degree rather than instead of one.

⚠⚠ Learn to build, not just to specify. BLS says AI may let people in other occupations do basic web tasks — that is already true, and the ground it does not reach is real applications.

And keep every syllabus. 181 course numbers across 25 prefixes with no course above 13 carriers means transfer evaluation in this subject is genuinely difficult, and the syllabus is the only thing that travels.

programs.note: The certificate and associate tier — 34 Florida public institutions, 1,133 credentials, ⚠⚠ and not one bachelor's degree. Valencia 276, Miami Dade 191. Cheap, local and good for building a portfolio; not the degree BLS says the occupation expects.

⚠⚠⚠ Where the bachelor's is. BLS gives a bachelor's as the typical entry for this occupation and the web CIP family awards none, so the degree-holders came through computing. ⚠ It is also the defensible ground against BLS's warning that AI may let others do basic web tasks — the answer is to build applications.

⚠⚠⚠ The comparison that should change somebody's mind: $104,000 here against $62,960 there, and BLS expects this occupation to grow 5% while graphic design declines 2%. ⚠ Closely related skill, very different market.

⚠⚠ The nearest operational neighbour and far more widely taught — 39 Florida institutions. The same CTS clock-hour courses appear in both, and the technical colleges teaching web design teach networking alongside it.

⚠ A real destination: EME6405 Educational Web Design is taught at four Florida universities, the field screens on a portfolio the same way, and training and development specialists number 452,300 with 43,900 annual openings and much-faster-than-average growth.

courses.reason: ⚠⚠ Web Security Specialist — 150 clock hours at 13 Florida technical colleges, and the MOST widely carried web course in the state. That the top of the list is clock-hour CTE rather than a degree course is the shape of this field.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Clock hours, not credit. Useful and cheap; it does not articulate into a degree by itself.

courses.reason: Web Design Fundamentals — 150 clock hours at 7 technical colleges. The entry block of the clock-hour route.
⚠ Web Interface Design — 150 clock hours at 7 technical colleges. The closest thing Florida's CTE system has to a named UX course.
⚠ Basic Web Page Programming — 8 institutions, the most widely carried COLLEGE-CREDIT web course in Florida. HTML, CSS and the foundations everything else assumes.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Florida numbers introductory web work at least four ways — COP2830, CGS2820, CGS1820 and COP2822 — none above 8 carriers. Register by number and keep the syllabus.

courses.reason: Web Authoring / Introduction to Web Design — 6 institutions. The same ground under a different prefix, which is the recurring problem in this subject.
⚠ Web Applications Programming — 6 institutions and upper division. This is the applications side BLS's warning does not reach, and it is the single most defensible course on this page.
Developing Web Sites Using PHP/MySQL — 4 institutions. Server-side work and databases, which is where page-building becomes application-building.
⚠⚠ User Interface Design / Human-Computer Interaction — 4 institutions, upper division. The academic core of UX, and the part that is research rather than decoration.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Also appears as human-computer interaction under the CAP prefix at other institutions. The subject is spread across 25 prefixes statewide.

courses.reason: Multimedia Web Interactive Designer — 300 clock hours at 8 technical colleges, part of the four-block DIG0081–0084 ladder totalling 1,050 hours.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ A CTE occupational completion point rather than a college course. It is a job title you can be hired on.

courses.reason: Introduction to Digital Media — 8 institutions including UCF. The college-credit bridge between the clock-hour and degree routes.

⚠ Introduction to Programming. Named because the whole argument of this page is that building beats specifying — and because BLS explicitly warns that basic web tasks are moving to people in other occupations.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Florida numbers introductory programming several ways (COP1000, COP2000, CGS1540).

courses.reason: ⚠ Introduction to Psychology — 33 institutions. Named deliberately: user research and interaction design rest on how people actually perceive and decide, and this is the cheapest serious grounding available.
Elementary Statistics — 39 institutions. A/B testing, analytics and usability measurement are statistical work, and the designers who can read the numbers win the arguments.
English Composition I — 39 institutions. Interface copy is design, and a portfolio is a written argument as much as a set of images.
Traditional and Digital Illustration — 8 institutions. Named because visual craft is still the entry ticket, and it is the part of design least displaced by generative tools.
